summary: Essex County, NY: enclosed wooden tower 1911, steel tower 1916; taken off the summit and re-erected in Speculator, where it now stands in a park.

facts.design: 40-foot steel Aermotor LS25 tower, replacing an enclosed wooden tower on the summit
facts.status_note: Not on the mountain: the tower now stands in Speculator, Hamilton County

access.note: The relocated tower stands in a village park in Speculator. The sources describe no access to the original summit.

visit.trail_note: The relocated tower is in Sacandaga River Community Park, not on Makomis Mountain; a visitor guide says you can climb it.

events.note: An enclosed wooden tower was built on the summit
Replaced by a steel 40-foot Aermotor LS25 tower; the newsletter gives 1912 for the first steel towers in the Adirondacks
Wooden steps added to the interior
Removed from the summit by private individuals sometime after 1970; the register gives the removal only as 1970s
Re-erected in the Village of Speculator by Excelsior Towers; a visitor guide dates the move to 2019
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register

corrections.why: The register says an enclosed wooden tower went up on the summit in 1911. The 1916 date belongs to the steel tower that replaced it.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 1911 for the wooden tower and 1916 for the steel tower. The newsletter says the first eleven steel towers in the Adirondacks went up in 1912. A Sun Community News article gives 1916 for the first steel tower in the park. The sources do not agree, so the story gives each date with its source.
The register and the lookout list tie the move to Speculator to 2022. The Adventures in New York guide says the tower was restored and moved to the park in 2019.

notes_for_editor: Dates conflict: built 1911 (register) against 1912 (newsletter) and 1916 (register's steel-tower date, Sun article). Relocation year conflicts: 2022 (register, lookout list) against 2019 (Adventures in New York guide). The brief's event text says LL25 and 'one of the first ten steel towers in NYS'; the register page says LS25 and does not make the 'first ten' claim, so I did not use it. A Sun Community News deck says the rebuild was 'at Lake Pleasant'; the other sources put it in Speculator, so I did not use that. The register page credits a 1917 photo to the New York State Archives; no image URL was found, so no photo entry. Removal year is only 'the 1970s' on the register; a search snippet mentions 1978 from an Adirondack Experience article, which I did not read, so it is not used. Confirm the park's current climbing rules with the village before any visit guidance is published. The summit site has no described remains; no field check was made.
